#2059. Atletico Madrid eye January move for Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Atletico Madrid are looking to make an ambitious January swoop for Martin Zubimendi after the Arsenal midfielder failed to convince Mikel Arteta to give him a regular starting spot.

The Spain international has started all seven of his Premier League appearances this season, coming off the bench. This has reportedly caught the eye of Diego Simeone, who wants to bolster his midfield in the winter window.

Atletico have marked Zubimendi as a possible target, according to Spanish radio station RNE via SPORT. Sporting director Mateu Alemany feels that there is still more to do with Simeone’s squad despite big investments in new players this summer.

If Zubimendi’s situation fails to improve at Arsenal, he could become one of the most wanted signings of January.

Zubimendi played a major role in Arsenal’s Premier League title-winning campaign last season. He made 34 league starts, scoring five goals and providing one assist.

He played a key role in the club’s run to the Champions League final. Since then Arsenal’s midfield has changed.

Injuries have hampered his campaign, but Myles Lewis-Skelly has returned to the midfield, and Bruno Guimaraes joined in the summer.

The 27-year-old has also expressed frustration at the lack of playing opportunities available to him. He was signed for £60 million from Real Sociedad to Arsenal just 18 months ago and has three-and-a-half years left on his contract.

Any move to Atletico would be a battle. Real Madrid are also reportedly fans of the midfielder, and he has also been linked with a move to Chelsea in recent months.

Atletico are keen to bring Zubimendi in alongside Pablo Barrios in central midfield.

It would be a dream combination for Simeone, and the Spanish club are willing to fund any move.

Another option could see him involved in a deal for Julian Alvarez. There are currently no talks about a potential swap deal.

Arteta has previously played down concerns about Zubimendi’s importance to Arsenal. Earlier this month, he highlighted the midfielder’s commitment and suggested injuries had affected his opportunities.

The Arsenal manager also made clear that Zubimendi would have chances to play, but would need to take them when they arrived.

That leaves the midfielder with an opportunity to work his way back into Arteta’s plans. However, Atletico’s reported interest could add another dimension to his situation as January approaches.

#2058. For Newcastle United fans who haven’t yet done so, I urge you to, because it’s excellent

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

“Hello, people of podland and beyond”, those were the words of fellow Mag writer Jamie Smith, as he introduced the inaugural episode of ‘The Mag Podcast’, back in August.

For those Newcastle United fans who haven’t yet listened, I urge you to do so, because it’s excellent.

We’re up to Episode 15 now and to date, Jamie has been joined for each episode by Simon Cahill, a southern convert to all things Newcastle United according to his Mag bio (he certainly sounds like he’s from down south) as well as the miserable mag himself, David Hutchinson, AKA Hutch (who sounds very much like a local).

Whilst Jamie and I have writing for The Mag in common, we don’t know each other and have only met each other in person once, but nonetheless, I have been heaping praise on him for most of the time after listening to each episode, including episodes 2 and 3, which I listened to high above the Atlantic Ocean as I flew in and out of New York on a family holiday (I reckoned that must have been a first for the pod).

I listen on Spotify, there are alternatives to this – Apple Podcasts, Amazon Music, YouTube if you like, and you can also play direct from the article that Simon routinely posts as each episode is released. I haven’t read a lot of comments from other Newcastle United fans about it, so it’s hard to get a handle on how The Mag Pod is being received. As I said earlier though, I think it’s marvellous.

During the past three months, the guys have navigated hugely important issues such as Manchester City’s alleged indiscretions with the 115 charges, and football’s loss of community with the increasing amount of commercial interests impinging on the beautiful game, as well as the possibility of new legislation to allow the consumption of alcohol in the stands.

Jamie, who speaks with a heavy Geordie accent but does so as eloquently as he writes, talked with passion to mark the passing of King Kev, The Mag podcast doing its very own tribute to the Messiah in episode 2.

I normally listen on my commute into work on the 21 bus. I often find myself laughing out loud, something that seems to make my fellow passengers extremely nervous from the looks I get when this invariably happens.

When discussing the 115 charges and potential punishments in episode 8, Jamie used the US justice system to illustrate how a massive points deduction for Man City would be as futile as those 500-year prison sentences they hand down in places like Alabama. That had me in stitches!

That was after Hutch had made a complete hash of introducing the Carabao Cup draw in episode 7, although in suggesting that we would lose to Fleetwood if we were to get them, he showed great foresight given that was Arsenal ‘s fate when they played at the other Highbury. Meanwhile, Simon was all over the place, when asked to read out the results from the Nations League matches during the international break.

In episode 9 (and you could tell that the International Break was grinding by this time) the guys even imagined themselves as Sam Beckett from the TV show Quantum Leap, in which they afforded themselves the opportunity to travel back in time in an attempt to change the course of history for Newcastle United.

The point here is that this isn’t easy, but they do a great job with humility and humour.

In the most recent episode (number 15) which has just aired, the lads gave their ratings on the season so far, Jamie and Simon going for D minus, with Hutch offering a marginally better assessment at D. I have to say, this did enrage me, particularly after my most recent article, ‘Lies, damn lies, and statistics (and Newcastle United)’ in which I made the case for Matthias Jaissle because we aren’t any worse off than last season and have in fact amassed a staggering five points more from our opponents these ten games into the season than was the case last time out in the corresponding fixtures. My own assessment, had I been asked – C plus (could do better but certainly not in special measures).

Had I also been asked to grade The Mag podcast, I’d be inclined to settle at a B; it’s still early days, but it’s improving week by week, the material is interesting, there is often humour and when I compare it to other Newcastle United podcasts I have listened to, I think it’s a whole lot better.

Call me biased if you want, but if you haven’t done so, give it a go and a big shout out to Jamie, Simon and Hutch, I’m already looking forward to episode 16. 🎙️ THE MAG PODCAST Ep 15: Fulham frustration, Newcastle United’s season report card and Relegation fears Listen to the latest episode of The Mag Pod! #2057. Arsenal’s Havertz penalty controversy sparks fresh call for change to football laws

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal’s controversial penalty claim against Hull City has raised new questions about how the offside rule is interpreted in football.

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher believes that whilst he understands why the officials made the decision, the result would have been different under the current rules.

Speaking on Ref Watch on Sky Sports, Gallagher said that the holding should have been the main focus of the incident involving Kai Havertz and Hull defender Nobel Mendy.

His comments have increased criticism of referee Farai Hallam and VAR official Michael Oliver. However, Gallagher also feels that the language used in the laws needs to be addressed to avoid this issue in the future.

The incident happened shortly before half-time during Arsenal’s 1-0 victory over Hull at the Emirates Stadium.

Mendy pulled Havertz’s shirt inside the penalty area, prompting VAR to recommend an on-field review. Hallam subsequently confirmed that the Hull defender had committed a holding offence.

However, he ruled that Havertz was in an offside position and awarded Hull a free-kick.

Gallagher believes that was incorrect under the laws of the game. He explained that being in an offside position does not automatically constitute an offence.

The player must be involved in play before the referee can give a penalty. In this instance, Havertz had not tried to play the ball or challenge an opponent before being pulled back by Mendy.

This means that the player was held first, so a penalty should have been given to Arsenal.

Gallagher said that the AR had first raised their flag for offside. He said that it was a great process with VAR, but the initial decision could have affected the outcome.

He recognised why the decision was made even though he felt Arsenal should have been awarded the penalty.

In terms of common sense, he said it does not look right to award the penalty, as Havertz was in an offside position and couldn’t legally contest for the ball.

But he emphasised that the officials must strictly enforce the laws of the game. Gallagher thinks there is some grey space here which can be addressed by having more specific wording.

This could be crucial in these types of situations as the difference between being in an offside position and committing an offside offence can have a big effect on whether a penalty is awarded.

It’s a small comfort for Arsenal after missing the chance to take the lead from the spot. But Martin Odegaard did eventually score the winner in the 72nd minute to give Mikel Arteta’s men three points.

The incident has exposed a wider problem for referees. Until the laws provide clearer guidance, similar decisions could continue to generate controversy.

#2056. Independent Football Regulator approve West Ham board appointment

The Independent Football Regulator has approved James Taylor as West Ham’s new CFO, who can now join the West Ham board as company secretary and a director.

He replaces Andy Mollet, who retired in the summer after 14 years at West Ham.

IFR Outcome: The IFR determined that James Taylor is suitable for the role of Officer at West Ham United.

James Taylor (the applicant) submitted an application to the IFR for approval to carry out the role of SMF3: Chief Finance Function at West Ham United Football Club Limited (West Ham United).

Having assessed the application, under section 29 of the Football Governance Act 2026 (the Act), the IFR has determined that the applicant is suitable to be an officer, SMF3: Chief Finance Function, of West Ham United.

This means that, having considered the factors in section 37 of the Act and the IFR’s ODSE Rules, the IFR has concluded that the applicant:

Under section 82 of the Act, a person whom the IFR considers is directly affected by an IFR suitability determination may ask for it to be reviewed by a committee of the IFR Board who were not involved in making the original determination.

Any request must be made within 7 days of this determination’s publication date (or, if earlier, the date on which the IFR notified that person of this determination).

Further guidance on who the IFR may consider to be directly affected by its determinations, and how to request a review, can be found here.

After any requested review has been conducted, a concerned person, or other person with a sufficient interest, has a further right under section 84 of the Act to appeal the reviewer’s decision to the Competition Appeal Tribunal.

The IFR was formed in 2025 and includes former West Ham Executive Director Tara Warren as a non-executive director on its board.

#2052. Arsenal Could Benefit as PSG Step Away from Ibrahim Maza Transfer Race

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal could have been given a helping hand in their quest to sign Ibrahim Maza. Paris Saint-Germain reportedly pulls out of talks with Bayer Leverkusen’s attacker.

The Gunners are just one of several clubs keeping an eye on the exciting young talent in Germany. However, with some of the biggest clubs in Europe keen on the prospect of adding the player to their attack, it might have made it difficult for them.

PSG looked like genuine contenders for the signing of Maza. The French champions having reportedly had talks with both Maza and Leverkusen.

It seems that PSG are not interested anymore, according to Fichajes. They have ended negotiations with the player and Leverkusen because they were unhappy with how the player’s representatives and Leverkusen have conducted themselves during the talks.

This could be great news for Arsenal, but it doesn’t mean they have full control of the situation.

The withdrawal of a club of PSG’s calibre is a benefit for Arsenal. They had seemed well on their way to landing Maza. Now, they will pursue him without the pressure of competition.

Maza has emerged as a good signing for clubs looking to improve the flair in their attacking third. Leverkusen will have noticed this and may be tempted to sell him if they get a decent offer.

Arsenal might also determine if Maza would be a valuable asset for their team in the long run. They must ensure that he can adapt to their attacking strategies.

They will not be the only one interested in Maza. Although PSG may be willing to let him go, there are many other clubs interested in the player.

Leverkusen will also want to get the best deal out of the situation. If they are willing to negotiate, Arsenal need to think if it would make financial sense to do so.

Finally, it will come down to what the player wants. Arsenal would need to persuade the player that the Emirates is the right place for his progression and that they can provide the right route for his aspirations and ambitions.

This may be a step in the right direction for Arsenal.

If Maza is still a target for the Gunners, then they may have a better chance of getting it done given PSG’s new stance. But they will still need to come to an agreement with Leverkusen and convince the player to move to north London.

#2051. Scott Parker Must Restore West Ham’s Most Dangerous Weapon

One of the most disappointing aspects of West Ham’s performance against Blackburn Rovers at the weekend was the fact that Jarrod Bowen didn’t drift into the middle and cause havoc in the way he had against Cardiff City. Having watched what happened in Wales, I was genuinely excited about the possibilities for our captain under Scott Parker.

Because make no mistake about it, one of the biggest reasons the Hammers were able to overturn a three-goal deficit against Cardiff was the freedom afforded to Bowen. No longer was he restricted to the right wing, and suddenly he was popping up in central areas of the pitch, having a hand in all three West Ham goals.

As a result, I thought we might have discovered something rather special. Bowen could start on the right wing but effectively be given licence to operate as a number ten, providing West Ham with a completely different attacking threat. It was a whole new Jarrod Bowen, and he was incredibly effective at it.

That’s why I was so disappointed to see Bowen playing as a conventional, orthodox right winger against Blackburn. Having witnessed how dangerous he could be when drifting into central areas, I really thought Parker would look to exploit that again.

Instead, Bowen spent much of the match operating in his familiar position, and West Ham lost the unpredictability which had made him so effective against Cardiff. Of course, Blackburn were different opponents, but I couldn’t help feeling we’d missed a trick.

West Ham captain Bowen looked brilliant when seemingly given a free role against Cardiff City

The interesting thing is that I don’t believe Bowen needs to become an out-and-out striker to solve this problem. In fact, moving him permanently into the number nine position could simply deprive West Ham of their best creative player.

What excited me against Cardiff wasn’t the prospect of Bowen replacing the centre-forward. It was the possibility of him playing both roles at different moments, starting wide before moving inside and creating problems that opposition defenders struggled to deal with.

For all West Ham’s attacking problems, we already have a player capable of making things happen. Bowen demonstrated that against Cardiff, and I would argue that his movement and creativity were every bit as important as the goals themselves.

There’s no reason why he cannot continue to provide width when required while also moving into the space behind the striker. That flexibility could be particularly valuable with Joël Piroe leading the line, giving West Ham somebody to finish the opportunities Bowen creates.

I don’t want to see Parker abandon something which worked so spectacularly after just 45 minutes. We’ve spent much of this season struggling to create chances, yet against Cardiff we appeared to stumble upon a way of getting considerably more from our best player.

The international break gives Parker time to work on these attacking combinations, and I hope restoring Bowen’s freedom is near the top of his priorities. By the time West Ham face Preston North End, I’d like to see our captain operating with the same licence that made him almost unplayable in Cardiff.

#2050. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

The final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Chelsea 4 Brighton 3 Leeds 1 Brentford 1 Sunderland 1 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 26%-74% BrightonShots: 17-15Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 4-7Touches in opposition box: 29-28

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

How many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

This is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:

#CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical issue. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 29%-71% BrightonShots: 9-6Shots on target: 4-3Corners: 2-4Touches in opposition box: 15-10

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

There has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

That is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

There was a fist pump from Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Stamford Bridge and we are moments away from kick-off in west London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this afternoon:

Chelsea: Martinez, Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill, Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Penders, James, Acheampong, Chavarria, Caicedo, Barco, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

Brighton: Verbruggen, Wieffer, Boscagli, Dunk, Vuskovic, Gross, Gomez, De Cuyper, Kadioglu, Yalcouye, Kostoulas.Substitutes: Steele, Struijk, Hadjam, Promise, Osman, Costinha, Cozier-Duberry, O’Riley, Oriola.

As you’d expect, there were big cheers for Emi Martinez from the Chelsea fans ahead of kick-off. He responded by shaking a fist in the air and giving them a big round of applause. This is his first game since the World Cup final for Argentina.

Chelsea had gone 77 League games without fielding a player aged 30 plus before handing goalkeeper Emi Martinez a debut today. The Argentine celebrates his 34th birthday on September 2. The last played aged 30-plus to appear for the club was Thiago Silva, who was 39 at the time.

“We are delighted to have him. To have a goalkeeper of his stature, his personality, I think he will bring a lot of qualities. I am sure he can have a straight impact. We spoke, he felt ready to play, so here we go.”

“We will see. It was a decision we thought was good for the team, for the club. Sometimes you have to take tough decisions because this one is an important one. But now we need to look forward.”

On Enzo Fernandez being left out of the matchday squad:

“We assess what is best for the team and considering everything, the situation, we need a team that is focused, with everyone involved that is fully committed and engaged with the game.”

Emiliano Martínez turns 34 on September 2 and by most tangible metrics, the goalkeeper is past his peak.

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea: Martinez, Fofana, Lacroix, Colwill, Neto, Gusto, Lavia, Hato, Palmer, Rogers, Joao Pedro.Substitutes: Penders, James, Acheampong, Chavarria, Caicedo, Barco, Gittens, Estevao, Welbeck.

“I am delighted to be at this football club,” Martinez said. “Coming to Chelsea, for me and my family, was an easy decision to make and I am just over the moon; I cannot wait to get started.

“I want to be successful here. I am someone who wants to win at everything I do and I want to bring that here to this football club because it is a football club that wins titles, so I think it is a good match. I am all passion and I play with my heart. I will give 100 per cent every game, every training session to make the club, my teammates and the supporters proud.”

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

Michael Carrick has now been sacked by Manchester United.

An official announcement on Thursday morning revealing the news.

Less than six months ago Manchester United agreed a contract with Michael Carrick for him to be manager until the end of June 2028.

The Geordie manager now the latest victim of Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers.

Manchester United now sitting in the relegation zone three months into the season.

Only one win in the Premier League this season, three in fifteen in all competitions.

The official Man U statement starting: ‘Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach. Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period. After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.’

The statement going on to add: ‘Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered. The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.’

It looks like Maurico Pochettino will be the new Manchester United team boss.

#2048. Arsenal Confirm 19 Players on November International Duty

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

There is no breathing space for the Arsenal squad. 19 players are going to represent their countries in international fixtures in the final break of 2026. Many will face crucial moments in the coming days with Nations League promotions and relegations still at stake.

There are plenty of important fixtures in November. A number of Arsenal players will be looking to help their countries qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals. However, whilst others will be battling to avoid relegation. A number of Gunners will also be facing their club teammates in some interesting fixtures.

One of the biggest matches will be the clash between England and Spain on November 15th in Madrid.

Spain includes David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino in their squad, meaning they could face five Arsenal teammates. Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Ezri Konsa are all in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad.

Spain lead England by three points in their Nations League group, but the Lionesses have a chance to keep their quarter-final hopes alive if they can defeat Croatia at Wembley on November 12.

Konsa will be absent during the first match as he undertakes personal training, but he could return in time for the encounter against Spain.

There is more Arsenal interest in Group A2. Jurrien Timber’s Netherlands facing Christos Tzolis’ Greece on November 13, followed by a clash with Kai Havertz’s Germany three days later.

Both the Netherlands and Greece are tied on eight points. Germany will be looking to move up in the standings against Serbia.

These games could affect how a number of Arsenal players come back into the fold with such a busy run of fixtures.

Viktor Gyokeres has the chance to help Sweden move up to League A.

The forward has scored four goals in four Nations League games. Sweden are two points clear at the top of their group. A win against Bosnia and Herzegovina on November 14 will guarantee them a promotion.

They then head to Poland for their final game. Gyokeres will be looking to continue his goal scoring and return to Arsenal with confidence.

However, Martin Odegaard will have a tough task ahead. Norway currently sit bottom of their group having only picked up three points from four games.

With three points behind second place Denmark, Norway will host Wales before heading to Denmark on November 17. Both games will be crucial for the Norwegians to avoid relegation.

Riccardo Calafiori will be on duty for Italy against France and Belgium. Piero Hincapie has two friendly matches against Ecuador, one against Costa Rica and one against Bolivia.

Bruno Guimaraes and Gabriel Magalhaes will be travelling to play against Japan and Singapore with Brazil. Kepa Arrizabalaga has received his first call-up to the Basque squad for their friendly against Venezuela.

James Scanlon could have a successful campaign with Gibraltar. Two wins against Andorra and Malta would see them top their group and progress to League C.

With so many Arsenal players playing in competitive matches, the international break could have an impact on a number of countries. Mikel Arteta will be hoping his players return in good condition before they resume their domestic campaign.

#2047. West Ham’s £20m Striker Has Two Weeks To Change Parker’s Mind

It would be fair to say that West Ham’s £20 million striker Pablo has been something of a victim of the club’s decision to sack Nuno Espírito Santo. As every Hammers fan knows, Nuno was a big fan of the Brazilian, who towards the end of his reign had moved to the top of the pecking order ahead of both Taty Castellanos and Joël Piroe.

Unfortunately for the former Gil Vicente forward, as soon as Scott Parker arrived, he dropped out of the squad altogether and didn’t appear to be anywhere near the first team. Pablo was absent from the matchday squads against both Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers, despite having been a regular selection under the previous manager.

There are two possible reasons for this, in my opinion. The first, and probably most obvious, is that Parker simply doesn’t deem him good enough to warrant a first-team squad place ahead of Piroe or Castellanos. The second could be the Championship’s squad eligibility requirements, with Soungoutou Magassa returning to the picture and potentially leaving Pablo as the overseas-trained player to miss out.

Now, I’m not going to sit here and pretend to be Pablo’s biggest fan. That would be disingenuous of me, because I’ve been critical of his finishing, overall technique and I still don’t believe he scores enough goals.

But let’s be fair, neither does Taty Castellanos, yet it always seems to be poor old Pablo who takes the brunt of the blame. Whatever his shortcomings in front of goal, nobody could reasonably question his work rate, which was clearly one of the reasons Nuno valued his pressing and willingness to chase lost causes.

The Brazilian could now be one of the unexpected beneficiaries of West Ham having so many players away on international duty. As things stand, Parker doesn’t have enough senior players available to put out a balanced eleven, even in a training match, which could provide Pablo with an opportunity to impress.

With Piroe representing Suriname and both of West Ham’s left-wing options, Manor Solomon and Edvin Austbø, also away with their countries, Parker has considerably fewer attacking players to work with than he would ordinarily expect.

Taty and Pablo will need to perform in training

It could therefore be that Pablo has a couple of weeks to impress his new boss, which in terms of effort and application I’ve little doubt he’ll do. The real question is whether Parker believes the striker possesses the necessary technique to operate within his preferred system.

After all, hard work should be a prerequisite rather than a reason for anybody to get into the team. And given Parker’s drive and intensity, I suspect everybody will be working hard once he has the opportunity to properly implement his methods.

But with West Ham’s pressing, or lack of it, also under the microscope, it could well be that Parker eventually chooses to select Pablo for exactly the same reasons Nuno Espírito Santo always did.

Pablo might not be the most technically gifted striker at the club, and his goalscoring record certainly leaves plenty to be desired. Nevertheless, if Parker wants somebody prepared to harass defenders, chase down possession and lead the press from the front, he already has a player who has demonstrated a willingness to do precisely that.

Whether that’s enough to earn him another chance remains to be seen, but the international break could provide an unexpected opportunity for a striker who appeared to have been completely forgotten.

#2046. Arsenal youngster suffers international injury setback

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Ceadach O’Neill has suffered a setback in his development after being ruled out of the Northern Ireland squad due to injury.

O’Neill had been named by Michael O’Neill in the squad for the last two games of the Nations League against Ukraine and Hungary. The 18-year-old was hoping to make his first senior start after appearing in four games for Northern Ireland, but all as a substitute.

However, he will miss the international break after suffering an injury. He was also unable to play in Arsenal’s Under-21s 5-2 win over Aston Villa on Sunday.

The news comes at a good time for the winger who has recently been getting more attention in Arsenal’s first team.

O’Neill has impressed Mikel Arteta in training with the senior players and has also made his first team debut in the Carabao Cup.

His performances have indicated he may be another academy player who will fight for a spot under Arteta. He also impressed during Arsenal’s loss to Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

The teenager was one of only a few players to leave the game with their head held high after providing Gyokeres with a good cross to bring the score back level.

He was also included in the Arsenal squad that travelled to Liverpool in the Premier League. Although he did not play, it was still a positive result.

The inclusion of the Northern Ireland call-up means he could continue to develop. Getting his first senior start would help him show he can perform outside of the academy.

O’Neill’s departure is a key moment for Northern Ireland. They still have much to play for in their final Nations League fixtures.

The squad sit one point above Hungary in Group B2 with Ukraine four points behind. They must now face Ukraine before they take on Hungary.

A first-place finish would guarantee promotion to League A. Finishing second would see them enter the promotion play-offs. With a promising young player leaving after the last international break, Michael O’Neill will be disappointed to lose him.

The manager praised O’Neill for his contribution to the squad and wished him a speedy recovery. The winger will now work on getting back to full fitness.

His recent inclusion in the first team, shows how far he has come in recent weeks. He will be hoping to get another chance when he is fully fit.

#2045. Amorim discusses post-Genoa pride, the Ramos ‘team problem’ and losing being ‘end of the world’

Ruben Amorim wants his AC Milan side to fear losing, while he believes Goncalo Ramos’ lack of goals is a team problem.

Milan got their seventh win in 11 Serie A games on Sunday afternoon as they overcame an in-form Genoa side 2-1 at the Marassi. Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic scored in the first half to put the Rossoneri in command, though Ellertsson’s late strike from range made it a nervy finish.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was a result and a response that was needed after the dismal defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday night, and it calms some of the turbulence before the international break. However, the search to become consistently good side is one that will continue in a fortnight.

Amorim spoke to DAZN not long after the final whistle to give his assessments on what was an important win for his side but one that they made hard work of in the end, with his words via MilanNews.

A response was expected after the Europa League, and it arrived. But it’s only the beginning. What positive things do you take away from this?

“I’m proud of my players. The most important thing was to be competitive, I said it before the match. If we approach every game like this, we’re one step closer to winning them all.

“There are times when you manage to play really well, but there are also times when we changed our approach and were strong on second balls and played a different kind of football. And that’s what great teams do: they play differently within the same game. I’m really pleased with my players today.”

“What I can say is that we can win every game, but I can’t guarantee we’ll reach that level of confidence by the end of the season. I don’t feel like we’ve got that kind of consistency yet.

“And I don’t want to say anything more than ‘we can win the next game’. Because that’s the feeling I get when I look at the team. But it depends on many things. If we’d had everyone available, we would definitely have been better in the Europa League, too.

“This run of matches has been tough for us with everything that’s happened. But I can say that if we’re competitive, then we can win every game in the league. Let’s focus on that and take it one day at a time.”

“It’s the mentality. When you’re a player, there are no off days. If you play for Milan, for these clubs, there are no off days. You can’t show up like you did on Thursday and then turn on again for Sunday. It’s not possible, it’s not something that will work.

“It’s not a physical condition, it’s a question of anxiety about defeat. If you ‘panic’ about defeat, it’s not that you’re afraid of losing, but that you know that losing is the end of the world. That’s the feeling I want my teams to have.”

How is Gonçalo Ramos’ development going? He got an assist today…

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#2044. West Ham’s £22m Question As Koppen’s Signings Come Under Scrutiny

Following information received by Claret & Hugh from a football agent that West Ham’s biggest problem has been recruitment, I thought it would be worth taking a closer look at the summer business conducted under Director of Player Recruitment Nils Koppen.

The argument that West Ham’s entire recruitment process needs rebuilding from the ground up is certainly an interesting one, and appointing somebody to oversee that operation is an obvious starting point. Koppen is effectively operating as a director of football, even if his official job title is slightly different, and his work will be crucial to the club’s future.

For the purposes of this assessment, I’ve concentrated on five players I understand to have been Koppen’s choices. I’ve left out Manor Solomon, Joël Piroe and Morato, whom I understand were specifically wanted by Nuno Espírito Santo, along with Keiber Lamadrid, who was already at the club last season and whose recruitment I understand was driven by David Sullivan.

It’s worth remembering that Koppen was hardly afforded the luxury of a full summer to plan his first transfer window. He arrived at West Ham on 4 July and explained in an interview with the club’s official Iron Cast podcast that his usual recruitment planning had to be dramatically accelerated.

Koppen described putting together an 80-day plan focused on executing the summer window, when ideally he would have preferred a much longer period to assess players and prepare. That’s important context when judging the business, particularly given the number of players West Ham needed to bring in.

Nevertheless, the signings are now here, and we’ve had an opportunity to watch them. It’s probably too early to place too much emphasis on any individual player, but we can at least begin to assess what Koppen has delivered and what supporters might expect from his recruitment in January.

I’ll start with Joël Veltman, who I think has been a really solid signing. He brings bags of experience, understands the defensive side of the game and would currently be my choice as West Ham’s best right-back.

Given that he arrived on a free transfer, I struggle to see how anybody could argue against this deal. Veltman was particularly impressive during the second half against Cardiff City, and his composure could become increasingly important under Scott Parker.

For me, this was an absolute no-brainer and one of the clearest positives from Koppen’s summer business.

Veltman has been a decent signing for West Ham

Unfortunately, I think quite the opposite can be said about Adama Boiro. He was clearly some way down West Ham’s list of preferred targets, and his failure to establish himself suggests this particular recruitment decision hasn’t worked.

I’m prepared to give the club a little leeway because I genuinely believe they expected El Hadji Malick Diouf to remain at West Ham for this campaign. That would have changed the urgency surrounding the left-back position and perhaps explains why the eventual recruitment looked rather improvised.

What is clear is that Nuno Espírito Santo didn’t appear to consider Boiro good enough for regular first-team football. I’d also be very surprised if he manages to break into Scott Parker’s starting XI, and therefore it’s difficult to regard his arrival as a good signing.

Divine Mukasa is a completely different proposition, and I think bringing him in on loan from Manchester City was an astute move. He’s clearly an exceptionally talented young footballer, and I believe there’s considerably more to come from him.

We’ve already seen glimpses of his ability, particularly during the comeback against Cardiff, when he scored and helped transform West Ham’s attacking play. He has the imagination and technical ability to make things happen, which is something this team has lacked far too often.

I actually think Mukasa could be one of the biggest beneficiaries of Parker having time to implement his ideas. Of course, the obvious downside is that he’s only on loan, but that doesn’t diminish the quality of the original recruitment decision.

Edvin Austbø is another player I think has enormous potential. The overall package was just under €15 million, but he’s on relatively modest wages, which is an important consideration when assessing the total cost of a transfer.

I’ve been encouraged by his directness, willingness to take on defenders and ability to make things happen. He looked particularly lively against Blackburn, and I was surprised when Parker decided to replace him with Manor Solomon.

There’s still plenty of development required, but that’s hardly surprising given his age. Austbø looks like a genuinely promising player, and if he continues improving, this could turn out to be an excellent piece of business.

His arrival also reflects the sort of recruitment markets Koppen knows well, with West Ham looking beyond the more obvious and expensive options for emerging talent.

Last but certainly not least is Arne Engels, the player from whom most is expected, and rightly so. At a reported £22 million, he became the most expensive signing in Championship history, so it’s perfectly reasonable to expect something special.

Nuno clearly liked him, and I suspect Parker will appreciate his qualities too. However, I’m still undecided about exactly what sort of player Engels is and what he does particularly well.

I would expect the most expensive player ever purchased in the Championship to excel at something, and I’m not entirely convinced Engels does. He’s a bit of an all-rounder, with bags of energy, decent passing ability and a willingness to get stuck in, but I’m still waiting to see that outstanding quality which justifies the fee.

That’s not to say he’s a bad player, because he certainly isn’t. He scored an excellent goal against Cardiff and has shown enough to suggest he could develop into a very useful midfielder, but I don’t yet know whether he’s the exceptional player West Ham paid exceptional money to acquire.

Indeed, if I could keep either Engels or Mukasa at the club next season, at this moment I’d actually choose Mukasa. That might change over the coming months, but it’s an indication of where I currently stand on the two players.

Overall, I think it’s fair to say Koppen’s first batch of signings has been a mixed bag. Veltman looks excellent value, Mukasa and Austbø have considerable potential, Boiro has been disappointing and Engels remains something of an unknown quantity.

However, I don’t believe we can reasonably judge somebody who is, for all intents and purposes, operating as a director of football after just one transfer window. Particularly not when he arrived with so little preparation time and was working alongside a manager who has since been dismissed.

I wouldn’t call Koppen’s recruitment a success or a failure at this stage. The jury is very much still out, and there’s every possibility that Austbø, Engels and Mukasa could enjoy excellent November and December performances under Parker.

If that happens, Koppen’s summer business could look considerably better by January without West Ham signing another player. Equally, if those players fail to develop, the questions surrounding his recruitment will become more difficult to ignore.

For now, it’s a case of watch this space. Koppen has made some encouraging decisions and some questionable ones, but his work deserves to be judged over a much longer period than a single summer transfer window.

#2043. The Premier League and The FA have now released this joint statement

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

The FA and the Premier League have released a joint statement.

The official release made public on Thursday morning.

The EFL and WSL also part of this joint statement.

The official statement beginning: ‘ The Premier League, The FA, EFL and WSL Football stand with all survivors of non-recent child sexual abuse in football and acknowledge the profound and enduring impact it has on the individuals and their loved ones.’

This statement then going on to detail: ‘The FA launched Voices of Truth, an acknowledgement of survivors’ courageous disclosures, which were a landmark moment in English football. Through the collective efforts of Clubs, Leagues, The FA and County FAs, we continue to make significant progress in strengthening safeguarding measures to promote and protect the safety and welfare of children, young people and adults at risk.’

The official release then going on to detail: ‘We have further deepened the provision of education and training, and strengthened how Clubs, academies and County FAs are audited and assessed. Reporting pathways are now more effective, and there is clearer oversight and accountability across the game. The annual Play Safe campaign continues to shine a light on the robust preventative measures now in place, highlighting the importance of children and young people’s voices as part of this work and reinforcing that safeguarding is a collective responsibility.’

The statement then adding: ‘Importantly, we also know that this work is never finished; it requires ongoing vigilance, steadfast commitment and bold leadership. We will never waver in our commitment to putting the safety and wellbeing of children and young people at the very heart of our work, while continuing to ensure that support remains accessible to all those affected by abuse.’

The joint release then giving out the following: ‘Information about confidential support services can be found here, with further information also available through Voices of Truth, a new, survivor-led digital platform hosted on The FA website. Any current safeguarding concern about a child or adult at risk should be reported without delay through the appropriate safeguarding reporting channels, or directly to the police in an emergency.’

#2042. Arsenal could use Berta connection to explore Endrick transfer

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal may be able to pursue a January move for Endrick. Andrea Berta providing a useful contact for the forward’s representatives.

A move to the Premier League is being linked with the young Real Madrid player after he failed to play regularly for his current Spanish club. As such, his representatives want to find a new club for him in the winter window.

With Bukayo Saka injured, Arsenal may be looking to strengthen their attacking options. Endrick’s ability to play in central areas and wide areas can make him an attractive option for Mikel Arteta.

But it’s not that simple. The North Londoners are not currently amongst the clubs who are pushing hardest to sign the Brazilian.

The TalkSPORT report that Berta’s links to Endrick’s representatives could provide Arsenal with an ideal starting point if they wish to pursue a deal.

The forward has been offered to a number of clubs in the Premier League as his camp seek to resolve his lack of opportunities in Real Madrid.

Arsenal are known to have been interested in the forward in the past. Newcastle United, Aston Villa and Tottenham are the clubs currently gaining more concrete attention.

It doesn’t mean they can’t make a move to north London. Berta’s connections may help them understand what is needed to get the player to the Emirates.

However, Real Madrid may be more reluctant to let the player go. The Spanish club have been reluctant to allow Endrick to leave before, making a loan look more of a realistic option.

Endrick arrived at Real Madrid with an incredible reputation having made his breakthrough at Palmeiras. However, due to there being competition for places, he has struggled to play much in Spain.

If he were to go to the Premier League, he would be able to play regularly to help his development. Playing under Arteta and competing for major trophies at Arsenal would be a great opportunity.

However, Arsenal would have to consider whether he would actually play enough. Moving to another team with competition for attacking spots may not be the best move for his development.

Arsenal need to decide whether Endrick would fill a real gap in their attacking line-up or simply add to their talented front line.

Although Saka’s injury makes attacking additions more important, they can’t make a decision based purely on the injury. They need to look at how he would fit into their future plans.

Thanks to Berta’s link, Arsenal can look into the possibility of signing him. Whether he is a serious target will depend on Real Madrid’s willingness to let him go and what Arsenal can offer him.

#2041. Füllkrug Admission Raises Uncomfortable Question About West Ham’s Striker Recruitment

Ordinarily, I wouldn’t be in too much of a hurry to pay attention to what Niclas Füllkrug says about West Ham. However, the fact that he currently tops the Bundesliga goalscoring charts with nine goals in nine games for Werder Bremen does lend some credibility to his latest comments.

Speaking while on international duty with Germany, Füllkrug has suggested that a lack of service was partly responsible for his struggles at West Ham and AC Milan. In an interview published by the German Football Association, he explained that his Bremen teammates actively look to find him with the ball, something he felt was missing at his previous two clubs.

The German striker cost West Ham £27 million when he arrived from Borussia Dortmund, and there’s little doubt in my mind that the Hammers failed to have a proper plan for incorporating him into the team. However, Füllkrug must also take his share of the blame because his first season was blighted by injury, and he also spoke about feeling homesick.

The truth is that Füllkrug was never really on the pitch for long enough for us to discover whether anything could have come from his transfer. His constant fitness problems made it almost impossible to establish any consistency, and he has now acknowledged that staying fit was the key issue during his time abroad.

That said, there is little in West Ham’s performances under Julen Lopetegui, Graham Potter or Nuno Espírito Santo that suggests we would have been able to get the best out of what is clearly a talented striker.

There may well be something in his assertion that he wasn’t given a decent supply line when he did play for West Ham. Indeed, we’ve previously looked at how Bremen have built their attacking play around Füllkrug, with teammates providing the service and support he so often appeared to lack in East London.

As for his fitness, I’m afraid that’s very much on him. West Ham have consistently demonstrated over the past few years that their medical team, physiotherapists and fitness staff have generally done a good job of keeping players available.

Füllkrug’s injury record was a significant part of the problem, and whilst it’s perfectly reasonable for him to question the service he received, it doesn’t explain why he spent so much of his West Ham career unavailable for selection.

Nevertheless, watching a striker who managed just three goals for West Ham now leading the Bundesliga scoring charts is bound to raise questions about the original recruitment decision. The fact that the club are still dealing with the financial consequences of his move only adds to the frustration.

Füllkrug has rediscovered his goalscoring touch at Bremen, and good luck to him. But I suspect the truth about his West Ham failure lies somewhere between the club not knowing how to use him and the player simply not being fit enough to give himself a proper chance.

Piero Hincapie has provided some good news for an Arsenal team that have struggled at the start of the season by confirming that he is now fully fit.

The defender has had two separate injury issues since joining Mikel Arteta’s squad but feels he is now over the setbacks and ready to play regularly.

Hincapie is playing for Ecuador in their November international fixtures. His inclusion in the squad was also a positive, as he was unable to play in their last camp due to injury.

Hincapie initially missed Ecuador’s September squad because of a groin problem. He had been named among the substitutes for Arsenal’s final match before that break, against Brighton.

After recovering, the 24-year-old returned to action in the 2-1 Premier League win over Leeds United on October 10. However, he suffered another setback during the warm-down after the match.

The ankle injury was particularly unfortunate, with Hincapie having to leave the pitch with assistance from goalkeeper Illan Meslier. He subsequently missed Arsenal’s matches against Lille and Nottingham Forest.

Mikel Arteta had at first suggested that Hincapie could be out for a matter of weeks, but the defender has since rejoined individual training.

#2038. Arsenal receive mixed verdict after Liverpool penalty review

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

We’ve an important update on the Arsenal Liverpool penalty decision. Arsenal received a mixed reaction from the Premier League’s independent panel after their controversial win at Anfield.

The panel were unanimous in their decision that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty after Jurrien Timber tugged Alexander Isak’s shirt. However, they were divided on whether it should have been reviewed by VAR.

The panel also cleared the officials on the incident involving Noni Madueke. This means that Arsenal were justified in their win due to the wrong decision being made on the penalty.

The incident happened during the 1-0 win for Arsenal at Anfield on November 1. Isak was trying to run onto a cross from Bradley Barcola after Kai Havertz had given the Gunners the lead.

As Timber pulled him back, he was unable to cleanly head the ball. The referee Andy Madley allowed play to continue. The decision was then made by VAR Stuart Attwell that there was not enough evidence to suggest a review.

The five-man Key Match Incidents panel has now ruled that this was the wrong decision. Four of the panel voted that Liverpool should have been awarded the spot kick after Timber’s handball.

However, there was a tight vote on whether VAR should have intervened. Three panellists felt that Attwell should have shown Madley to the pitchside monitor, whilst two felt it did not reach the threshold.

One panellist felt the length of the hold was not long enough to affect the movement of Isak. The other two members who felt that VAR should not have intervened also said that it is subjective as to how much the hold would affect the striker.

This is an important point to note. Whilst they agreed that the penalty was deserved, there was less agreement on whether it was VAR’s responsibility to overturn the decision.

There was also good news for Arsenal in the panel’s decision regarding Madueke’s late altercation with Alexis MacAllister.

The Liverpool midfielder fell to the floor following a headbutt from the Arsenal winger. The incident was reviewed by the VAR, but Madueke was spared a red card. Mac Allister received a yellow.

All five panel members agreed that Madueke should not have been sent off. They felt that there had not been any contact, and Mac Allister’s reaction was certainly excessive.

It certainly gives us an alternative standpoint into the situation. Whilst Arsenal benefited from the incorrect decision regarding the penalty, the officials were backed up with the disciplinary incident.

This won’t have any impact on the result of the Anfield game, as Havertz’s goal was the winning goal and gave Arsenal their first league victory at the stadium in 14 years.

However, it does show how risky Timber was to make the challenge and how close the panel were with whether they should have intervened with VAR.
