#2037. Any three of these seventeen Premier League teams could be relegated this season

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Looking at the 20 Premier League teams this season, which ones do you think will end up relegated?

I think it is a tough one, a really tough one…

We appeared to have reached a point where it was looking all but impossible for clubs to come up from the Championship and survive.

In the 2024-25 season, all three Premier League teams that had been promoted from the Championship in May 2024 were all relegated with a pitiful number of points. They only picked up 59 points in total from their 114 collective fixtures with Leicester 25 points, Ipswich 22 points and Southampton 12 points, they won only 12 Premier League matches between them.

It is early days but from a total of 30 collective attempts this season, you have Ipswich, Hull and Coventry having picked up eight wins and seven draws between them and 31 points.

One or more of them may well end up relegated but I don’t think any of that trio are guaranteed to go down this time, immediately after having escaped from the Championship.

The current Premier League table on Thursday 12 November 2026

I honestly think that it is a case of any three from the following seventeen Premier League clubs who will be relegated.

Aston Villa Bournemouth Brentford Chelsea Coventry Crystal Palace Everton Fulham Hull Ipswich Leeds Manchester City Manchester United Newcastle United Nottingham Forest Sunderland Tottenham

Apart from Arsenal, Brighton and probably Liverpool, I don’t think any of the Premier League teams are safe.

By this point after ten games of the 2025-26 Premier League season: Eight Premier League teams had 17 or more points (this season only four have 17+). There was a gap of 16 points between 5th top and 20th (this season only nine points). Twelve Premier League teams had won at least four matches (this season seven).

I am guessing that some of you are puzzled about the inclusion of Manchester City, but if/when their appeal fails against the 114 guilty verdicts on breaches of Premier League rules, every chance that relegation will be the key punishment.

Put it this way, only Hull and Coventry are seen by the bookies as more likely to be relegated than Manchester City.

Last season you needed 40 points for safety, with West Ham ending the season on 39 points in 18th place.

Plenty of people will think it is impossible for say Manchester United to be relegated, when they have such huge advantages on almost all other Premier League clubs when it comes to their ability to spend on transfer fees and wages.

If Manchester United hadn’t fluked a home win against Aston Villa on the final day of the 2024-25 season they would have finished on 39 points. Before that Villa match Man U had only won four of their last 21 EPL games and picked up 17 points. Considering they only have one win and eight points from their first ten Premier League games this 2026-27 season, what if Manchester United had a similar end to this campaign as they had two seasons ago?

The Premier League is so competitive this season, so many teams can beat each other, pretty much anything is possible…

Arsenal have made contact with Bournemouth over a potential move for Alex Scott. Mikel Arteta may have to rethink his transfer plans if competition for the midfielder intensifies.

According to The i Paper, Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all made exploratory enquiries about the 23-year-old. The clubs want to establish what it would take to persuade Bournemouth to sell. However, none appears close to agreeing to a deal.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on a summer move. Liverpool and Chelsea are more interested in signing Scott in January. However, if they were to make a serious offer, it could be hard to hold out.

Scott has become one of the most exciting midfielders in the Premier League. He is an attractive option for clubs looking to improve their squad going forward due to his age, experience and being a homegrown player.

However, there is some uncertainty around Scott’s future. The England international has turned down two contract offers and is unwilling to sign a new deal. There are 18 months left on Scott’s contract, meaning it is an increasingly important decision for Bournemouth.

Arsenal are interested in Scott with doubts surrounding their own midfield options. There have been reports linking Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino to exits.

Scott would give Arteta another option, but Arsenal will have to consider if they want to make a move and give Liverpool and Chelsea an advantage.

Bournemouth are reported to want more than £100m to let him go during the January transfer window.

It would be a big asking price, especially given that Scott has 18 months left on his contract. There are a few reasons why Bournemouth could be holding out for a big fee.

The Cherries had to pay £25m to bring Scott in from Bristol City, who will receive 20 per cent of any future transfer fee. They will also have to find a suitable replacement at the halfway stage.

Reports said Chelsea received a number of offers worth around £70m in the summer, but Bournemouth have rejected claims that a bid of £80m will get them talking.

Scott is believed to be happy to stay at the club until the end of the campaign. Bournemouth are also having a great season under Marco Rose, currently sitting in seventh place in the Premier League with eight straight wins in all competitions.

Arsenal have little to hurry into any deal and could use the summer to negotiate a better deal. This is especially true with Scott’s contract situation becoming more of an issue.

The problem is that Liverpool and Chelsea are keen competitors and could lead to a bidding war in January, leaving Arsenal with little room to negotiate.

Whilst Arsenal have made their interest known, this doesn’t necessarily mean he will be moving anytime soon. If Scott is a genuine target, then they must be prepared to pounce if the situation arises.

Former Premier League goalkeeper Jussi Jääskeläinen thinks David Raya is the best goalkeeper in the division right now.

The Spaniard has played a key role for Mikel Arteta since his arrival from Brentford. His organisation of the backline, key saves and contribution to Arsenal’s build up play have helped him to be a standout player.

In 2012, Raya began his journey in English football when he moved to Blackburn Rovers from Spain. At that time, he was just a young teenager unfamiliar with English football.

His short spell at Southport introduced him to senior football. Soon, he returned to Blackburn and forged a career ahead of moving to Brentford in 2019. After four years with Brentford, Raya achieved success at the club, helping them to the Premier League.

The player’s performances in the higher leagues caught the attention of Arsenal, and Arteta signed him on loan to the Emirates in 2023 before making the move permanent the following summer.

It didn’t take long for Raya to establish himself in the team. He took home the Premier League Golden Glove, having achieved 16 clean sheets in 32 appearances.

Raya has already proven he can play to the top standard. However, it will be his consistency moving forward that will define his long-term reputation.

This shows that his playing time has not affected his relationship with Arteta.

Merino was able to understand what it is like to be a manager because his father was a football coach. He understands that tough decisions have to be made when selecting your starting XI.

This can be an important aspect in a difficult season, as all players need to play their part to make sure Arsenal stay challenging in multiple competitions.

Merino’s comments are very interesting considering the uncertainty around Zubimendi.

There are reports Zubimendi has been linked to Atletico Madrid and whether he will be looking to move in January.

Merino didn’t give a definite answer that these players will stay at Arsenal, but the comments do suggest they are looking to improve their position in the squad.

He also underlined the importance of having good cover, with Spain boss Luis de la Fuente believing players coming off the bench can be just as vital as those starting.

This is something Arsenal will want their squad to take on board. They will not always be able to play the same midfielders due to the demands of playing in both domestic and European competitions.

There is still time for Merino and Zubimendi to turn their situation around, so what they are doing now may not indicate how important they are going to be in the campaign.

Arsenal will be keen to keep Merino happy, and he has made his position clear. This should give some reassurance ahead of the January transfer window.

#2029. West Ham’s Leadership Problem Goes Far Beyond Championship Experience

West Ham’s lack of Championship experience has been highlighted by former striker Sam Parkin, who believes the Hammers are missing the know-how required to negotiate difficult away matches.

Speaking on the Sky Sports EFL Show, Parkin questioned whether West Ham have enough experienced organisers in the team, with The72 highlighting his concerns about a midfield containing Arne Engels, Mohamadou Kanté and Divine Mukasa.

Let’s be absolutely clear about this. West Ham lack leaders, full stop. I believe this is partly a consequence of Graham Potter’s clear-out, something highlighted in Michail Antonio’s book, with the former manager appearing to move on some of the bigger personalities at the club. And let’s be fair, they’ve not really been replaced.

However, I think there are two separate issues here. One is leadership, while the other is tactical nous, and I’m not convinced they’re necessarily solved by the same player.

If West Ham are looking for somebody prepared to scrap, they really need look no further than Edson Álvarez. The Mexican is already at the club despite having been frozen out under Nuno Espírito Santo, and he would immediately bring some bite to the midfield.

From a tactical point of view, I suspect Scott Parker will persevere with Soungoutou Magassa in defensive midfield once he gets back up to full fitness. Parker has already brought him back into the picture, and a specialist defensive midfielder could make a significant difference to how West Ham cope when games become physical or untidy.

Longer term, though, there is little doubt West Ham should be looking at the personalities they’re recruiting, not simply the technical ability of individual players.

When Director of Player Recruitment Nils Koppen assesses potential January signings, I’d like to think he’ll be considering whether they can organise those around them, take responsibility and provide leadership when things aren’t going well.

Parkin makes a fair point about Championship experience, but for me the issue goes deeper than knowing the division. West Ham have lost too many big personalities without replacing them, and that’s something Parker and Koppen will eventually have to address.

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Sunrise on Thursday 12 November 2026, all 20 Premier League managers who were at their clubs when the 2026-27 season kicked off were still in their jobs.

Then just like waiting for the bus, two come at once.

In the space of two hours today, a couple of clubs sacked their Premier League managers.

Manchester United sending Michael Carrick on his way this Thursday morning, then Crystal Palace doing the same with Pierre Sage very soon afterwards.

That is two of three clubs in the Premier League relegation zone having sacked their managers so far in this international break, with Sunderland second bottom is Regis Le Bris safe?

The 2026-27 season is still trailing the 2025-26 campaign though, as by this time four Premier League managers had been sacked by early November 2025.

At the same though. there was then a two month gap between the start of November 2025 and start of January 2026 before a fifth top tier manager was sacked.

In total, eleven Premier League managers were sacked during last (2025-26) season (with their replacements in brackets):

9 September 2025 – Nuno leaves Forest (Ange Postecoglou) 27 September 2025 – Graham Potter leaves West Ham (Nuno) 18 October 2025 – Ange Postecoglou leaves Forest (Sean Dyche) 2 November 2025 – Vitor Pereira leaves Wolves (Rob Edwards) 1 January 2026 – Enzo Maresca leaves Chelsea (Liam Rosenior) 5 January 2026 – Ruben Amorim leaves Man U (Michael Carrick) 11 February 2026 – Thomas Frank leaves Spurs (Igor Tudor) 12 February 2026 – Sean Dyche leaves Forest (Vitor Pereira) 29 March 2026 – Igor Tudor leaves Spurs (Roberto de Zerbi) 22 April 2026 – Liam Rosenior leaves Chelsea (Caretaker boss for rest of season) 30 April 2026 – Scott Parker leaves Burnley (Caretaker boss for rest of season)

#2027. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2024. West Ham Linked With Swansea Star As Magassa Exit Rumours Emerge

West Ham United have been linked with a January move for Swansea City midfielder Marko Stamenić, although I must admit I’m struggling to see why another central midfielder would be a priority for the Hammers.

According to Keith Haynes of Swansea Independent, both West Ham and Southampton are monitoring the 24-year-old New Zealand international. The report suggests Stamenić’s passing ability and defensive awareness have attracted attention, although no formal approach has been confirmed.

West Ham supporters might remember the midfielder from our 1-0 victory over Swansea in October. Stamenić was dispossessed by Divine Mukasa in the build-up to the winning goal, with the young Hammer eventually finishing the move himself. However, that particular incident is hardly a reason to judge a player’s overall ability.

Personally, I think the last thing West Ham need at the moment is another central midfielder. I can think of at least four positions that require strengthening before we start looking to add more players in that department.

We’ve already got Arne Engels, Divine Mukasa, Mohamadou Kanté, Lewis Orford, Tomáš Souček and Soungoutou Magassa, among others. Indeed, the number of midfield options available has been a talking point throughout the season.

More interestingly, the Swansea report also suggests that Magassa could leave West Ham in January, although that remains unconfirmed.

West Ham paid Monaco approximately £20 million for Magassa, but his lack of involvement under Nuno Espírito Santo has hardly helped maintain his transfer value. I would suggest that his valuation has depreciated significantly since arriving at the club.

Given that Scott Parker immediately brought Magassa back into his starting line-up against Cardiff, there is at least some indication that the new manager sees a role for that type of defensive midfielder.

Scott Parker scouted Magassa during his time at Monaco

For me, the sensible approach would be to get Magassa involved in the first team, build up his match fitness and see whether Parker can coax the performances out of him that persuaded West Ham to spend £20 million in the first place.

That would give us a better player and potentially restore some of his transfer value, rather than selling him at what could be a considerable loss.

Stamenić may well be a decent enough footballer, and his reported statistics at Swansea are encouraging. But unless there is a significant departure from West Ham’s midfield, I really don’t see the logic in spending more money on a position where we already have plenty of options.

Surely there are more pressing problems for Nils Koppen to solve in January.

#2023. Liverpool player who Iraola has largely ignored is told he needs to ‘get back into shape’

One Liverpool player has been told by the current coach of his national team that he needs to ‘get back into shape’ if he’s to earn an international recall.

The most recent of Federico Chiesa’s 51 caps for Italy came two months before he joined the Reds from Juventus in August 2024, and the forward has struggled for game-time at Anfield under both Arne Slot and Andoni Iraola.

So far this season, the 29-year-old has been given a mere two minutes of matchday action by the Basque, coming on at the end of the defeat to Manchester City after recovering from a back injury in the early weeks of the campaign.

There have been reports that Liverpool are increasingly open to selling their number 14 in January if the right deal can be struck, and Azzurri head coach Roberto Mancini has told the player what he must to do in order to get back into his country’s squad.

The former Man City boss said (via Liverpool Echo): “As far as Federico is concerned, I have already spoken with Federico several times, including recently.

“Right now, he isn’t playing and needs to regain his fitness and get back into shape; but he is a 29-year-old player, still in the prime of his physical maturity, so I believe he can return with us very soon.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Mancini is leaving the door open for a potential Italy recall for Chiesa in the future, but it isn’t helping the forward’s case that he’s hardly getting a look-in at Liverpool.

He’s only been in the matchday squad for four of our 16 matches so far this season and has now been leapfrogged by Lewis Koumas in the pecking order up front, with Iraola demonstrably preferring the Welsh youngster over the 29-year-old.

The Azzurri boss travelled to England a few weeks ago in the hope of seeing long-time injury absentee Giovanni Leoni in action, which suggests that he has the Reds defender firmly in mind for the national team when the teenager is back playing again.

Mancini hasn’t forgotten about Chiesa either, but the message from the tactician is clear – our number 14 needs to regain match sharpness, and right now his chances of doing that at Liverpool seem nonexistent.

With that in mind, it wouldn’t surprise us if the popular Italian forward were to depart in January, but not before winning the affection of Kopites and playing his part in our Premier League triumph under Slot two seasons ago.

#2022. West Ham Fanzine Blowing Bubbles Shortlisted for National Award

West Ham might be lumbering in mid-table but Hammers fanzine Blowing Bubbles is very much top of class after it was shortlisted for Fanzine of the Year at the 2026 Football Supporters’ Association Awards.

It’s the fourth time the publication has received the recognition, having previously been nominated in 2015, 2021 and 2023. Blowing Bubbles joins five other finalists, including Sunderland’s A Love Supreme, Leeds United’s The Square Ball and Middlesbrough’s Fly Me To The Moon.

Editor David Blackmore launched Blowing Bubbles in the summer of 2012 and has been involved ever since. The publication celebrated its 100th edition in February 2020 and has now reached issue 173, which is quite an achievement for an independent monthly football fanzine.

“I’m absolutely delighted that Blowing Bubbles has been shortlisted for Fanzine of the Year for a fourth time. To be in such an elite group of fantastic football publications is a massive pat on the back and recognition of not only the huge amount of time and effort we put into producing every issue but also to the continued support we’ve had from the West Ham Family.”

Anyone involved in producing independent football content will appreciate the work that goes into keeping a publication going month after month. Credit must also go to David’s team of writers and designer Kelvin Farrell.

The winners will be announced on Monday 30 November at London’s Nobu, Portman Square, with Victoria Derbyshire hosting the FSA Awards. The fanzine category will be decided by a judging panel.

From all of us at Claret & Hugh, congratulations to David and the entire Blowing Bubbles team. Best of luck on awards night. Fingers crossed you bring the trophy home!

#2021. De Rossi praises Genoa’s performance, Amorim as a head coach and Milan’s ‘world class’ duo

Daniele De Rossi has revealed that he congratulated his Genoa players despite their defeat against AC Milan this afternoon.

Milan did what they had to do after their midweek setback against Ferencvaros at San Siro by securing a much-needed three points to move back into the top four in the Serie A table, at least for the time being. It was not a given either, against a Genoa side who had won three in a row and four in five.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Both goals came in the first half as Alphadjo Cisse continued his excellent scoring form by firing in Adrien Rabiot’s cut-back. Christian Pulisic buried Goncalo Ramos’ square ball to double the advantage, and Ellertsson scored late to make it a tense finale, but Milan got over the line.

De Rossi was interviewed by DAZN (via MilanNews) after the full-time whistle at the Marassi to give his opinion on what was largely a positive performance from his side, but not the result to match.

Did you throw it away with individual mistakes?

“I congratulated my players. The performance was very good. I don’t like to talk about individual errors. I hear so many coaches talking about individual errors when they concede goals, not when they score. Kalulu also made an individual error on Baldanzi’s goal [against Juventus].

“That’s football. We can’t just rely on it when it suits us. There are ways to correct mistakes. We all made some mistakes collectively on the goals; we could have done better, but overall, I think the game was very good.”

It was an excellent reaction from the team despite going two behind…

“Before the last break, we were a bit more fragile, but my players always reacted. We were orderly in our reactions. Milan have a couple of players who hide the ball from you when it’s hot, but it never gets hot for them.

“They make you lose a bit of distance, and you have to put in a game that requires a lot of physical sacrifice. Everyone did it, and it makes me realise I have a team to be proud of. If we play like we did today, we’ll win more games than we’ll lose.”

“I shouldn’t judge him: he’s younger than me, but he has a lot more experience than me. I learn from him. We study him, we watch him. He plays with a system I really like.

“He puts a lot of quality on the wings, something I’ve also tried to do here. Certainly not Moreira’s level, but with the right proportions and possibilities.

“I like the way he communicate, he doesn’t blame his players even when they lose, he’s always honest when they lose. He’s doing an excellent job.”

“For anyone who loves this post, it’s exciting to see this player paint football like this at 41. Last season I had him man-marked, this season he played with two. He has more time on the ball.

“Maybe he goes a little slower, but the thought goes. We’ve clashed a couple of times and I told him, ‘I don’t play anymore so I can’t beat you’. But he’s beautiful, truly beautiful. He’s like Rabiot: world-class players.”

#2020. West Ham’s £5m Winger Has Gone From Match-Winner To Liability

Whilst most concentrated on Mads Hermansen’s inability to make saves during West Ham’s 2-1 defeat to Blackburn Rovers, it allowed somebody else to escape the glare of criticism. That player was Manor Solomon, because, to put it frankly, he was awful when coming on as a substitute to replace Edvin Austbø at Ewood Park.

The Israeli international has been shocking for West Ham recently, ironically since the last round of international fixtures in September and October, when he represented his country four times and returned to East London looking completely knackered. His performances have deteriorated to the point where I struggle to see what he’s currently offering the team.

We now find ourselves in the rather strange situation where, with West Ham entering another international break, we’re hoping Solomon can go away with Israel and somehow regain some form. Because as things stand, he is simply not a viable option in the current West Ham team.

No doubt West Ham manager Scott Parker, being something of a Championship expert, would have had reasonably positive opinions of Solomon, having witnessed him tearing up the division for Leeds United during their promotion season. However, he’ll have been left in no illusion that the version of Solomon he’s inherited since replacing Nuno Espírito Santo is a long way from that player.

Solomon stunk the place out in the first half against Cardiff City before being substituted, and when introduced in place of Austbø against Blackburn, he made the team noticeably worse. It’s particularly frustrating because Austbø had looked lively and dangerous, offering the directness and attacking intent that Solomon currently seems unable to provide.

Nuno Espírito Santo pushed hard for the signing of Manor Solomon

It’s important to remember that, whilst West Ham haven’t spent a fortune bringing him in, Solomon was signed for a reported £5 million precisely because he was supposed to guarantee goals and assists in a Championship team. Unfortunately, that looks a long way off at present, and the attacking contribution we expected simply hasn’t materialised consistently enough.

Solomon has been called up by Israel for two UEFA Nations League fixtures during the November international break. He will face Kosovo away on Saturday 14 November before Israel take on Austria in Debrecen, Hungary, on Tuesday 17 November.

The winger also featured in all four of Israel’s September and October Nations League matches, so another spell of international football is hardly guaranteed to leave him refreshed. Nevertheless, West Ham and Scott Parker will be hoping those two games can kick-start Solomon into something approaching his previous form.

There is clearly a talented Championship player in there, as he demonstrated during his time at Leeds. But the player who was supposed to provide West Ham with goals, assists and attacking quality is currently struggling to make any meaningful impact.

Parker has the international break to work with much of his squad, but Solomon will be away with Israel rather than spending that time on the training pitch with his new manager. Perhaps a change of environment and a couple of international appearances will do him some good, because West Ham desperately need the Manor Solomon who helped Leeds win promotion, not the one we’ve been watching recently.

#2018. West Ham Youngsters Send Parker Message With Juventus Victory

West Ham United’s Under-21s produced an impressive performance to beat Juventus Next Gen 3-1 at Victoria Road last night, with three different players getting on the scoresheet in the Premier League International Cup.

Harry Montague, Tyrone Omotoye and Jethro Medine scored for the Hammers, who recovered from conceding an equaliser just before half-time to claim their second victory in three matches in the competition. The result moves Mark Robson’s side up to third in Group A with six points.

However, perhaps the most interesting aspect of the evening came from Robson’s comments afterwards. With Scott Parker now in charge of the West Ham first team, the academy coach made it clear that he hoped some of his youngsters had caught the attention of the senior coaching staff.

According to the official West Ham match report, the Hammers dominated much of the opening half and took the lead in the 29th minute.

Preston Fearon delivered a dangerous free-kick into the penalty area, where Montague was on hand to finish from close range.

Juventus equalised through Marco Tiozzo in the 43rd minute, but West Ham continued to create opportunities after the break.

Omotoye restored the lead in the 58th minute, finishing clinically from Jephthah Medine’s cross, before Jethro Medine converted a stoppage-time penalty to complete a thoroughly deserved victory.

Robson was particularly pleased with the contribution of several younger players who had stepped up from the Under-18s.

Speaking to the club’s official website, Robson said:

“We were miles better on the ball than we have been in recent games. I was really pleased with the performance.”

The former West Ham midfielder also highlighted the increased energy and aggression his side displayed compared with their previous defeat against Monaco.

However, it was his final observation that stood out.

“Hopefully, one or two of the lads impressed the first team staff that might have been here this evening.”

It’s an interesting comment given the recent managerial change at West Ham.

As Claret & Hugh recently reported, Robson returned to his Under-21 coaching role during the summer after previously working with the senior squad.

That experience should put him in a good position to judge which youngsters might eventually be capable of making the step up.

There have already been encouraging signs from young players in the first team this season, and Parker will undoubtedly be keen to assess the talent available throughout the club.

Of course, performing well against Juventus Next Gen is very different from playing Championship football. Nevertheless, the academy continues to provide reasons for optimism.

The result also follows another impressive European performance against Valencia earlier in the competition.

West Ham’s next International Cup fixture is against Jong Genk in December, while Robson’s side return to domestic cup action against Brighton Under-21s on 23 November.

#2017. West Ham Face Solomon Fitness Scare Ahead Of Preston

West Ham United winger Manor Solomon is struggling with back pain while on international duty with Israel, raising fresh concerns about his fitness ahead of the Hammers’ Championship clash with Preston North End.

According to Israeli publication Walla Sport, Solomon was only able to complete part of Wednesday’s training session ahead of Saturday’s Nations League match against Kosovo. The winger participated in the opening stages before withdrawing from the remainder of the session.

A further report on Thursday morning suggested that Solomon remained a doubt for the fixture, with his fitness due to be assessed again. There has been no confirmed withdrawal from the Israel squad, but given his recent problems, this is hardly the news West Ham supporters will have wanted to hear.

I am fully aware I might be contradicting myself here, having previously wanted Solomon to play for his country as a way of kick-starting his West Ham form. But this injury concern does cast the situation in a completely new light.

I understand that the left winger is an important player for Israel, but as I’ve made the case repeatedly, I believe his poor form is a direct result of him being overplayed by his country during the last international break.

Indeed, Claret & Hugh reported Solomon’s back problems during the October international break, when a club source confirmed that the winger was suffering considerable pain.

And if he is injured, or even feeling some pain in training, there is no way he should be risked against Kosovo.

There is simply too much at stake for West Ham to have a player returning from international duty in a worse physical condition than when he left.

That said, I do think Edvin Austbø has moved ahead of Solomon in the pecking order to start against Preston on West Ham’s left wing.

Solomon has struggled to find his best form, while Austbø has been pushing hard for an opportunity to impress new gaffer Scott Parker. Even if both players return fully fit, I would be inclined to give the Norwegian the starting place.

But with the competition in the EFL Championship starting to get very serious, I do hope that West Ham officials will be on to the Israel national team, pleading with them not to play Solomon unless he is 100% fully fit.

There is no suggestion at this stage that Solomon will miss the Preston match, and hopefully this turns out to be nothing more than a precaution.

However, given what happened during the previous international break, surely the sensible thing is to avoid taking any unnecessary risks.

Andy Robertson has said that there were two Liverpool matches in particular last season that he ‘hated’, having been left with a ‘headache’ after both.

The Reds were beaten twice by Galatasaray in the 2025/26 Champions League, with a pair of 1-0 defeats at RAMS Park in the league phase in September and the round of 16 first leg in March (Arne Slot’s team won the return fixture 4-0 a week later).

Both matches were almost clones of one another, with the Merseysiders conceding an early goal and being unable to restore parity after putting in a subdued performance.

Now of Tottenham Hotspur, Robertson reflected on the two visits to Istanbul last season and how he was left with a migraine from the incessant intimidation from the natives.

The Scottish left-back said (via Fanatik): “I hated playing against Galatasaray last season. The Galatasaray away game was terrible. They booed non-stop throughout the entire match. Believe me, you leave the match with a headache.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The city of Istanbul has left an indelible mark in Liverpool’s European history from the epic 2005 Champions League final against AC Milan, but recent visits to the Turkish capital have been bruising.

The Reds twice relinquished a lead to lose 3-2 away to Fenerbahce last week, and the two trips to play Galatasaray last season were galling, to say the least.

Pat Nevin justifiably claimed that the 1-0 league phase defeat ‘could have been worse‘ given the nature of our defending that night, and John Aldridge described the repeat of that scoreline in the knockout phase eight months ago as a ‘horrible watch‘.

Slot had warned about the febrile atmosphere of RAMS Park prior to the latter fixture, remarking: “Sometimes you wonder if this could be done by human people”, and for a player of Robertson’s character and experience to be so rattled by the intensity of the home support is quite telling.

With Galatasaray currently 18th in the league phase standings, it’s not inconceivable that they and Liverpool could meet at some point in the knockout rounds yet again next spring, but we’d imagine that the Reds have had their fill of visits to Istanbul after the past 14 months.

#2014. Scott Parker Has Two Weeks To Solve West Ham’s Pressing Problem

West Ham have been given a fairly clear indication of what to expect from Preston North End when the two sides meet after the international break. Preston manager Graham Alexander has been explaining the aggressive pressing approach that helped his team beat Southampton, and it’s something Scott Parker will undoubtedly need to consider.

Speaking to the Lancashire Evening Post following the victory, Alexander said: “We pressed everything.” Preston outshot Southampton 12-3 in the first half, and their manager intends to use the break to reinforce that approach.

Without wishing to belittle Preston’s performance against Southampton, I have to say West Ham are in big trouble if we can’t beat them, irrespective of what their press might be. We can analyse the opposition’s tactics until we’re blue in the face, but ultimately West Ham should have enough quality to overcome Preston.

Parker has two weeks on the training ground to drill his players, and I would expect that time to be significant. He’s barely had an opportunity to work properly with the squad since replacing Nuno Espírito Santo, something that was evident during the defeat at Blackburn Rovers.

Parker has a philosophy of wanting to keep the ball, so I suspect he’ll want West Ham to play their way through Preston’s press rather than simply bypassing it with long balls. Of course, that requires players who are comfortable receiving possession under pressure and know where their next pass is going.

I also believe we’ll see a specialist defensive midfielder, such as Soungoutou Magassa, used more often than not for the remainder of the season. Parker has already shown a willingness to use Magassa, and having somebody in that position could prove particularly important when opponents attempt to press West Ham high up the pitch.

Preston’s victory over Southampton was a decent result, but it doesn’t suddenly make them an opponent West Ham should fear. Quite frankly, if the Hammers can’t beat the likes of Preston in our own backyard we don’t deserve to get promoted.

Parker has been given a valuable fortnight to work on his methods, and the expectation has to be that we return from the international break looking considerably better organised.

Whether Preston press high, sit deep or alternate between the two, West Ham need to be capable of dealing with it. That’s the challenge facing Parker, and I don’t think it’s an unreasonable expectation.

#2013. Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

Little sorcerer calls time on playing for his country six weeks after World Cup final defeat which was marred by brutality of his team-mates

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. You can find him on X at @oliverbrown_tel.

Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

#2012. West Ham’s Interest In Sydie Peck Resurfaces After Summer Pursuit

West Ham United have once again been linked with Sheffield United midfielder Sydie Peck, with transfer journalist Ekrem Konur reporting that the Hammers are continuing to scout the 22-year-old.

The England Under-21 international has attracted attention from several clubs, with Newcastle United and Sunderland also named in the report. Peck has certainly done his reputation no harm recently, scoring a hat-trick against Preston North End earlier this month, although there is no suggestion that West Ham have made a formal approach.

Interestingly, this isn’t the first time Peck has been linked with a move to the London Stadium. ExWHUEmployee reported through The West Ham Way back in July that West Ham had been monitoring the midfielder even before the arrival of director of recruitment Nils Koppen.

I looked quite closely at Peck during the summer when West Ham were first linked with him, and I have to say, he was a player who caught the attention.

Back then, however, we didn’t know who was staying and who was going, and the midfield situation was very different.

Since then, West Ham have signed Arne Engels and retained Soungoutou Magassa, while Mohamadou Kanté has emerged as one of the most encouraging performers of the season.

I think Peck is a decent player. Very good, in fact, and somebody who would be extremely useful in the Championship.

But unless there are due to be significant outgoings, I just cannot see this one happening.

Kante has become an important player for West Ham

Lewis Orford is not getting enough game time as it is, and Mohamadou Kanté is having one hell of a breakout season. I wouldn’t particularly want to bring anybody in who might stop that.

And let’s not forget the point Nils Koppen has made about West Ham’s recruitment strategy: the club don’t want to sign players who block the pathway of youngsters coming through.

It’s a philosophy I agree with, particularly when we’ve got young players already showing that they deserve opportunities.

There is clearly something about Peck that West Ham’s recruitment department likes. After all, the interest was being reported before Koppen arrived, and his performances for Sheffield United have only strengthened his case.

But there’s a difference between identifying a good player and identifying a player you actually need.

West Ham have more pressing areas of the squad to strengthen, and unless Scott Parker is expecting a major shake-up in midfield, I’d be surprised to see the club pursue this particular deal in January.

#2009. ‘If I stayed…’ – Rio Ngumoha reflects on ‘no-brainer’ decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool

Rio Ngumoha has said that his decision to swap Chelsea for Liverpool in 2024 was a ‘no-brainer’.

The Reds signed the teenage winger from the London club’s academy just after he turned 16, with a subsequent tribunal determining that the Merseysiders were to pay an initial £2.8m (potentially rising to £6.8m) in compensation.

The now 18-year-old has gone on to make 44 appearances and counting for LFC’s first team, along with winning three senior England caps, and he’s turned in some man-of-the-match performances at Champions League level.

In a recent media interview (via The Standard), Ngumoha explained that he decided to leave Chelsea for Liverpool because he saw a clearer pathway to the first team at Anfield than he did in west London.

The winger said: “I needed a new challenge. I feel like if I stayed at Chelsea… not saying I wouldn’t have got to the first team as quickly, because I believe in my ability, but I feel Liverpool just gave me a new pathway.

“The plan they set for me was straightforward. For me, it was a no-brainer going to Liverpool.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The Reds have had a fine track record for attracting top-class teenage talents in recent years, and Ngumoha is perhaps the standout signing in that category.

That Liverpool were prepared to go through a rigorous registration process with the Premier League (as the winger was a minor at the time) shows just how determined they were to see the deal through, and all of that bureaucratic effort has proven to be more than worth it.

In little more than a year, the teenager has gone from highly-rated prospect to established first-team presence, and there’s a palpable excitement among the fans at Anfield every time he gets the ball, with many a defender bamboozled by his phenomenal dribbling ability and supreme self-confidence.

Ngumoha’s leap of faith in joining the Reds has been vindicated by his regularity of senior football, especially this season as he’s started almost half of our matches across all competitions, and full credit to him for seizing his opportunity when it’s been handed to him.

Chelsea’s loss has very much proven to be our gain, and with the 18-year-old now holding a market value of €50m (£41.8m), that aforementioned compensation fee looks increasingly like one of the steals of the century.
